examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Row-major indexing makes the last index vary fastest. For R×C arrays, element offset is iC+j, multiplied by element size for a byte address. A contiguous declared multidimensional C array differs from a separately allocated pointer-to-pointer structure. Traversal order affects locality without changing logical dimensions. Bounds are checked mathematically in exam reasoning: adjacent physical memory does not legalize an out-of-bounds C access.

**Key relationship:** Row-major A[R][C]: offset(A[i][j])=(i·C+j)·element size

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Write dimension strides.
2. Convert element offsets to byte offsets.
3. Distinguish contiguous arrays from pointer tables.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For row-major arrays, rightmost indices vary fastest: A[i][j] has element offset iC+j in an R×C array. Compare access order with page/cache block size. A column loop can revisit more distinct pages than available frames even when consecutive rows share a page.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A zero-based int A[10][20] has four-byte elements and base address 1000. What is the address of A[3][7]?

**Answer: 1268.** Element offset=3·20+7=67. Byte offset=67·4=268. Address=1000+268=1268. The column count 20, not the row count 10, determines row stride.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Partial C aggregate initialization zero-fills unspecified elements. Reading beyond an array boundary remains invalid even if adjacent memory happens to exist.

Array capacity and the number of currently stored elements are separate quantities.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Zero-based row-major A[4][6], two-byte elements. Byte offset of A[2][3]?

- **A.** 15
- **B.** 18
- **C.** 30
- **D.** 36

**Answer: C.** Element offset=2·6+3=15, so byte offset=15·2=30.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Rightmost index varies fastest in row-major layout
- **B.** Array bounds remain relevant even if nearby memory exists
- **C.** A contiguous 2D array is necessarily identical to separately allocated int** rows
- **D.** Byte offsets require element size

**Answer: A, B, D.** Pointer tables and contiguous rows have different representations and type rules.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

A[8][10] uses four-byte elements and base 2000. Address of A[5][2]?



**Answer: 2208.** Element offset=5·10+2=52. Address=2000+52·4=2208.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q57 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/arrays?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Virtual memory and page replacement. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. A page holds 512 array elements, or four complete rows of length 128. The array spans 128/4=32 pages.
2. For a fixed column i, consecutive groups of four row accesses touch pages 0 through 31. The first access in each group faults; the next three hit. Only 30 frames are available.
3. Each column revisits a page after accessing the other 31 pages, so LRU has evicted it. Thus every column incurs 32 faults: 128×32=**4096**.

#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q42 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/arrays?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Arrays and multidimensional storage. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. len1 tracks the trailing run of equal values, while len2 tracks the longest valid two-value suffix. If the new element is second rather than first, the two-value suffix extends but its equal-value run resets to 1: P=1.
2. If a third value arrives, only the previous final equal-value run can be kept alongside it; the new valid length is old len1+1. Thus Q=len1+1.
3. The correct pair is **B**.
